narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A warm day climbs toward a high of 30°C / 86°F, while the sky shifts from early Mostly clear to midday Mostly cloudy and stays Mostly cloudy into the evening. thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. The wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning south-southwest by midday and southwest into the evening, with gusts up to 35 km/h (19 kt) ashore and 27 km/h (15 kt) on Winam Gulf. The ultraviolet index peaks at 9.3. Air quality is forecast at AQI 79 from the model estimate. As of 06:01, reports through 05:30: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C / 70°F; low so far 20°C / 68°F; peak sustained 6 km/h; sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS bring a continuation of today’s warmth. Tuesday will be Partly cloudy, Wednesday Partly cloudy, Thursday Mostly cloudy, Friday Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy, Sunday Mostly cloudy and Monday Partly cloudy. Models show rain possible each day, with Thursday (Day+3) at 100% probability and Monday (Day+7) also at 100%. Highs range from 30 °C to 31 °C on Thursday and settle around 29 °C to 30 °C by Monday. The record notes ECMWF as the best rain caller for Day+3.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

The peak CAPE values—UKMO at 2650 J/kg, ICON at 1800 J/kg, ECMWF at 1530 J/kg and Best Match at 1940 J/kg—signal the potential for thunderstorms today, especially in the evening. Such storms could produce sudden gusts well above the forecast wind, posing a rapid-change hazard.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), turning south-southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), and becoming west-southwesterly into the evening at 14 km/h (8 kt) gusting 25 km/h (13 kt); peak gust reaches 27 km/h (15 kt). If thunder develops, gusts may exceed these values, adding a storm-related wind hazard.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) – a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days, and pressure is also falling toward the northwest and west. Pressure overhead is falling. Basin pressure today sits between 1012.9 and 1015.0 hPa, near-steady over three days with a -1.4 hPa trend. The pressure trend is –0.9 hPa, with the lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review finds no single model clearly ahead at Day+0, though Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind, and ECMWF under-forecasts both. The record shows GFS as the best rain caller for Day+0, yet GFS does not see today’s thunderstorms coming. The Call’s high of 30 °C matches the model spread, while its peak gust of 35 km/h (19 kt) aligns with the higher end of model gusts. Kenya Meteorological Department forecasts the same high and low temperatures, agreeing with the Call, though it provides no thunder guidance. Data sufficiency notes 60 checks for the least-covered model at Day+0, giving a settled picture despite uneven KMD coverage.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Thursday, with rain possible from Thursday and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday, then mostly cloudy Thursday. Rain gains support through Thursday, from two of four models Tuesday to all four models Thursday. Thursday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 80% of the time over 79 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms possible Friday and Saturday, showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Monday. Friday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 6 mm on average, highs 29 to 31 °C, thunder possible rather than likely. Saturday: all four models wet, highs around 30 °C. Sunday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 29 to 31 °C, thunder likely rather than possible.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Saturday. GFS is the wetter solution from Friday to Saturday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Monday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 75 checks.
